column1: # Golden routing corpus for agent-lint.py --eval
# Columns: task<TAB>expected_agent<TAB>class          (class optional, default `contract`)
# expected_agent is a roster agent name, OR the sentinel "LOW" meaning the
# router must return LOW/NONE confidence (the "commission an expert" path).
# WHY THE CLASS COLUMN EXISTS. Until 7.16.0 this file was one undifferentiated
# set and --eval printed a single number: "top-1 accuracy 100.0% (55/55)". That
# number was true and it measured almost nothing. 46 of the 55 scored rows were
# a verbatim vocabulary subset of the very agent they were supposed to select —
# the tasks had been written from the triggers. Exactly one row shared less than
# half its vocabulary with its target. A corpus co-authored with the artifact it
# scores measures mutual consistency, not routing ability, and a single combined
# percentage hides which one you are looking at. So the classes are reported
# SEPARATELY and never averaged together:
#   contract        Task vocabulary drawn from the agent's own triggers. This is
#                   an acceptance contract for the trigger set: it proves a
#                   trigger still selects its owner. It is NOT evidence the
#                   router generalizes, and must never be quoted as accuracy.
#   paraphrase      Real-world phrasing of the same need, authored WITHOUT
#                   consulting any agent's routing_triggers. This is the only
#                   class that measures generalization. Abstention (LOW/NONE) is
#                   a CORRECT outcome here — the router is a keyword heuristic
#                   and saying "no clear specialist" is the designed answer when
#                   it has no signal. What must not happen is a confident wrong
#                   answer, because the kernel tells briefs to cite the band as
#                   evidence.
#   adversarial     Phrasing built to bait a plausible-but-wrong specialist.
#   unknown-domain  Expected LOW: nothing on the roster is written for this.
# PROVENANCE of the paraphrase rows: authored 2026-09-13 during the 7.15.0
# remediation audit, from the real-world description of each task, before the
# router was changed and without reading the triggers of the agent each row
# names. They were NOT adjusted afterwards to make the router look better —
# tuning triggers against this set, or moving a failing row into `contract` to
# protect a headline number, is the specific dishonesty the class column and
# agent-lint's overlap check exist to prevent. The overlap check FAILS the lint
# if a row labelled `paraphrase` is in fact a near-copy of its target's
# vocabulary, so the label cannot be quietly wrong.
# Owned/extended by `tester` + `data-ml`. Seed for the production
# .claude/agents/_routes.golden.tsv.

# INFLECTION ROWS (7.16.0). Two rows below are existing contract rows with one
# word put into a different form. They are here because the corpus could not see
# a defect that reached a third of the router's vocabulary: `STEM = 6` tested
# whether the TASK's word prefixed a roster word, which a plural never does, so
# `nodes` scored zero against `node` and `checked` zero against `check`. Every
# row in this file was written in the same base forms the triggers use, so the
# whole corpus shared the blind spot it exists to measure.
# A whole `inflected` CLASS was built and then thrown away, and the measurement
# is why: 18 hand-derived inflected rows all passed BEFORE the fix as well as
# after, and an exhaustive search over every single-word inflection of every
# contract row found 22 that change the verdict, of which exactly 2 are
# grammatical English. A class of 18 rows where 16 pass either way is coverage
# to look at, not evidence — so the two real ones are here as ordinary contract
# rows, and the vocabulary itself is measured directly and exhaustively by
# tests/test_router_reach.py, which asserts 0% of either router's vocabulary is
# unreachable by its own plural. A sentence samples; that test enumerates.
# Still missing, and named rather than faked: the BAITED-AND-REWORDED cell.
# `adversarial` holds 12 fixed phrasings and `paraphrase` holds reworded but
# unbaited ones; nothing measures a bait row restated in other words, which is
# where the router is weakest. Filling it honestly needs an author who has not
# read the triggers — see the PROVENANCE note above — which the 7.16.0 author
# was not. docs/plans/router-lexical-reach.md §4 S5 carries it as open work.

# The class was declared in CORPUS_CLASSES, in SPEC-0002 and in this header
# and carried ZERO rows, so "confident-wrong = 0 in every class" was true of
# it only because it was empty. Each row below leans on vocabulary that
# belongs to one agent while the work belongs to another; the expected value
# is the agent that should actually do it.
# Authored 2026-09-13 by reading each agent's triggers and deliberately
# borrowing them for a task they do not own — the opposite of the paraphrase
# set, and the reason these are NOT held-out evidence of generalization.

#  But `pentest`'s description says outright that `security` "owns
#  design-time threat models", and ui-ux-designer's charter never
#  mentions threat modelling. The screen is what is being modelled, not
#  the deliverable. Expected value corrected to `security` — and note
#  the row was scoring as confident-CORRECT before, which means it was
#  rewarding the router for taking the bait.)
